bull.b: Large, consistent operating cash flow and material free cash flow provide durable funding for network investment, dividends, and buybacks. With OCF covering net income (~1.39x) and rising FCF guidance, the company can sustain strategic investments and shareholder returns over the medium term.

Top-tier NPS and repeated third-party network awards signal a durable competitive advantage: better acquisition, lower churn, and higher-quality adds. Network superiority supports pricing power, CLV improvement and sustained market share gains across consumer and enterprise segments.

Rapid FWA net adds, healthy ARPUs, and product ecosystem traction (T‑Life MAUs, co-brand card success) diversify revenue beyond handsets. Broadband and services expansion increases higher-margin, recurring revenue and creates stickier customer relationships over the medium term.

bear.b: High debt-to-equity reduces financial flexibility to pursue opportunistic investments or weather rate shocks. Even with strong ROE, elevated leverage increases refinancing and interest-rate exposure and constrains optionality for large strategic moves over the next several years.

Anticipated large spectrum auctions create structural capital allocation tension: management must reserve cash for bids, potentially limiting buybacks or incremental network investments. Auction outcomes could materially affect growth and competitive positioning depending on spectrum cost and success.

Planned wholesale roll-offs and documented prepaid subscriber declines signal structural revenue headwinds in lower-margin channels. Persisting softness there could slow overall service revenue growth and require higher acquisition effort or price innovation to offset lost volume.
